question:
During a data-checking activity, two real quantities $x$ and $y$ are recorded through the equations $2x+3y=18$ and $4x+6y=r$, where $r$ is the second recorded result. The students observe that the coefficients in the second equation are twice those in the first equation. They must decide which recorded values of $r$ produce compatible information and which value produces a contradiction.

(a) Calculate the determinant of the coefficient matrix.

(b) Determine the value of $r$ for which the system is consistent.

(c) For this value of $r$, express the solutions using one parameter and state their number.

(d) Examine the system when $r=40$ and justify the conclusion.
explanation:
(a)
The coefficient matrix is
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3\\4 & 6\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$|A|=2(6)-3(4)=12-12=0$$

(b)
The left-hand side of the second equation is twice the left-hand side of the first equation. For consistency, its right-hand side must also be twice $18$. Hence,
$$r=2(18)=36$$
Therefore, the system is consistent when $r=36$.

(c)
When $r=36$, the two equations represent the same relation:
$$2x+3y=18$$
Let $y=t$. Then,
$$2x+3t=18$$
$$x=9-\frac{3t}{2}$$
Thus, the solutions are
$$x=9-\frac{3t}{2},\quad y=t,\quad t\in\mathbb{R}$$
The system has infinitely many solutions.

(d)
When $r=40$, the equations are
$$2x+3y=18$$
$$4x+6y=40$$
Dividing the second equation by $2$ gives
$$2x+3y=20$$
The same expression cannot be equal to both $18$ and $20$. Therefore, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

options.A:
(a) Determinant $0$
(b) $r=40$
(c) $x=10-\frac{3t}{2},\ y=t$; infinitely many solutions
(d) For $r=40$ the system is consistent
options.B:
(a) Determinant $12$
(b) $r=36$
(c) $x=9-\frac{3t}{2},\ y=t$; one solution
(d) For $r=40$ the system has infinitely many solutions
options.C:
(a) Determinant $0$
(b) $r=36$
(c) $x=9-\frac{3t}{2},\ y=t,\ t\in\mathbb{R}$; infinitely many solutions
(d) For $r=40$ the system is inconsistent and has no solution
options.D:
(a) Determinant $0$
(b) The system is consistent for every $r$
(c) $x=9-\frac{3t}{2},\ y=t$; infinitely many solutions
(d) For $r=40$ the system has a unique solution
